rv.q: After the interval Maria Friedman's production feels much more nimble and immediate.
But not even Friedman’s ferocious eye for detail and the cast’s formidable energy can disguise the fact that the musical itself is a bit of a mish-mash tinged with snobbery.
Style and finesse don't figure on the agenda, from the minute the show shuffles haphazardly into gear.

This production is a great credit to the original film and actors, and has everything you could want from a musical: unforgettable music, extraordinary dancing and an uplifting feeling that will stay with you for days.

cn.t: A stylishly directed but dramatically flawed Cole Porter musical that dazzles with exuberant performances and classic songs, though critics split on whether the show's energy overcomes its uneven source material and patronizing story.
